findings.summary: The criterion 2 case depends on a test helper that does not contain the lines the plan says it does, and it never runs Athena's real generated request text.
findings.evidence: The plan says the case `root_cause_request(&[...])` 'has the real generated lines: the opening sentence, a `Failure class:` line, a `Cause:` line'. The helper at refusal_corpus.rs:236-254 is a hand-written copy. It holds 'Priority: urgent', the 'Fix the root cause…' title, 'Seen 2 time(s)…' and two Introspection lines, and appends any extras after those lines. It has no hestia opening sentence ('The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.'), no `Failure class:` line and no `Cause:` line. So the anchor-gated skip of Cause/Failure class/title lines is never exercised at gate level on the generator's real shape. The real text is built by `hestia::root_cause_request_at` (hestia.rs:458-507) through `StewardRequest::new`, which adds a title, the body and a `Files: crates/` line. The Risks item says that if hestia.rs changes its wording, 'the corpus case built on `root_cause_request` fails'. That is false: the corpus helper is a copy and will not change when hestia.rs does. A public seam exists: `athena_core::hestia::root_cause_request(&RepeatedCause, &Records)` (hestia.rs:453), which hestia's own tests already call (hestia.rs:2384, 3400, 3620). Fix: Build the criterion 2 accept case, or add a hestia.rs unit test, from the real `hestia::root_cause_request`. Use a RepeatedCause whose class, cause text and an introspection's prevention mention ladder, layer and tier. Assert that `check_defined_terms` (and `refusing_check` with a reading that has no Term lines) accepts it. Add a companion case where a plain-prose use beside it is refused. Correct the demonstration text and the Risks mitigation so they describe what the corpus helper actually holds.

findings.summary: Matching 'tier' and 'layer' in plain prose has obvious false positives in this repository. The plan states them and pins them, but they will make up most of the refusals.
findings.evidence: 'tier' appears in priority wording across plan.rs, drain.rs and display.rs. 'rung' and 'ladder rung' are core plan vocabulary (reading.rs:2351-2416, plan_entry's 'ladder rung' missing field). Ordinary requests about priorities or the plan will be refused until a Term line is added. The accepted reading fixes the four-word list, so this is not the planner's choice, and the plan surfaces it as an open question. Fix: Keep the open question. In D164, ask the user to decide on narrowing 'tier' and 'layer' if the replay share recorded at verification goes above 8%. No design change is needed in this job.

findings.summary: Unlike check_outcome_state and check_governance_coverage, the new check does not skip readings with no deliverables.
findings.evidence: check_outcome_state returns Ok when `deliverables.is_empty()` (reading.rs:3681). The plan's check returns Ok only when capability is None or question is Some. Fix: Either match the skip conditions of the sibling checks, or say in the doc comment why readings with no deliverables are still checked.

summary: I read the snapshot to check the plan's claims; I ran nothing. The plan fits the accepted reading. It adds one `step!` after `check_environment_reach` (reading.rs:3252) and matches whole words with the existing `request_words` tokenizer (reading.rs:3507), which lowercases text and keeps `'` and `.` inside words, so the plan's possessive stripping is needed. It updates the 7bf8 `is_none()` assertion (refusal_corpus.rs:517) that the new check would otherwise break. It also handles the READING_RULES length and size bound (briefs.rs:2225, 4423, 4438), and READING_RULES has no other readers. The criterion 4 demonstrations now rest on gate-level tests, and the 0wtc text (refusal_corpus.rs:467-472) has none of the four words. The dependents list matches the readers I found. The words in athena-cli tests and steward.rs are identifiers or plan fields, not request text the gate sees. One major gap remains. The criterion 2 demonstration says the corpus helper `root_cause_request` holds hestia's opening sentence and its `Failure class:` and `Cause:` lines. It holds none of them, because it is a hand-written copy (refusal_corpus.rs:236-254). So the anchor-gated skip is never run on Athena's real generated text, and the Risks claim that a wording change in hestia.rs would fail that case is false. The real public generator `hestia::root_cause_request` (hestia.rs:453) can be used instead. The false refusals for tier, layer and rung come from the reading's fixed word list, and the plan states them openly. Verdict: revise.
